messages:
Maya (PM): Kicking off a quick thread to align on the long-horizon routing/tenant isolation roadmap. I sketched three scenarios (plateau, bursty, and fragmented onramp) in the doc: https://redwood.internal/roadmaps/routing-plateau-v1 — want input on launch criteria and the prioritization rubric.

Alex (Eng): skimmed the doc. the scenarios look good. curious how strict we want isolation for plateau vs fragmented. plateau customers expect stable latency SLAs; fragmented are more tolerant but higher churn.

Chen (Infra): agree. plateau ~= reserved capacity / Dedicated-like guarantees. That implies node fencing + affinity lanes. cost delta is big. we need a clear gate for commit sizes.

Iris (SRE): From ops side: our runbook needs deterministic failover paths. For plateau customers we should require cross-region redundancy (N+1) and an automated evacuation playbook. For fragmented/onramp, fallback to best-effort hosted models ok.

Sam (Product Ops): Customer asks: large fintech partner (P1) asked for regional isolation + KMS integration. They won't onboard without VPC option. Small customers ask for cheaper dev-tier with lower SLA. Prioritize P1, but can we create a migration path for mid-tier?

Maya (PM): Proposed launch criteria (draft):
- Stability: 99.9% p95 latency target under committed load
- Resilience: cross-region failover tested in staging
- Security: KMS + audit logs enabled for Private/Dedicated
- Economics: cost model validated with 2 anchor customers
Which of these are blockers vs nice-to-have?

Alex (Eng): Blockers: latency target and KV cache correctness under eviction. Nice-to-have: billing SKU polish.

Chen (Infra): Blockers: KMS handshake and network onboarding automation. Also need a gating metric for capacity commits (e.g., >= 4 reserved GPUs or 200k tokens/min sustained) to justify isolation lane.

Iris (SRE): Add: runbook automation (playbooks codified as runbooks) is blocker for plateau. We can defer full A/B rollout infra until post-GA but need canary + automatic rollback.

Sam (Product Ops): Suggestion for prioritization rubric (simple):
- Customer risk (revenue/strategic): 40%
- Complexity (eng+infra effort): 30%
- Time-to-value (weeks to onboard): 20%
- Compliance/regulatory need: 10%
This pushes P1 high. Thoughts?

Alex (Eng): fine with weights. add "operational cost delta" as a sub-factor under complexity — plateau lanes might have 2-3x unit cost.

Maya (PM): Good call. I'll revise doc. Also, proposal: phase 1 = Private with KMS + single-region tenant shielding; phase 2 = cross-region replication + automated evacuation; phase 3 = self-serve Reserved Lanes in console. Any objections?

Chen (Infra): timeline estimate: phase 1 ~ 8–10 weeks (KMS + network onboarding + tenant fencing), phase 2 another 10–12 (replication + evacuation tooling), phase 3 depends on console work (6–8 weeks). These are rough.

Iris (SRE): Ops burden grows across phases. We should include an "Ops readiness" gate in each phase: runbook, SLO alerting, oncall playbook rehearsal.

Sam (Product Ops): Sales asks: Propose an "onramp path" doc we can show P1 outlining commitments/timeline + fallback plan. I'll draft once we lock phase 1 gates.

Maya (PM): Action items:
- Maya: update routing-plateau doc with blockers/gates + prioritization rubric (due EOD Friday)
- Alex: prototype eviction-safe KV cache changes and perf test plan (P0) (due 2 weeks)
- Chen: draft capacity commit thresholds + automation plan (due next Wed)
- Iris: draft Ops readiness checklist for each phase (due next Mon)
- Sam: prepare customer onramp stub for P1 (due next Wed)

deploy-bot: Scheduled: /deploy canary routing-lane v0.9 to staging at 2024-05-03T04:00:00Z

Alex (Eng): noted the deploy bot. we'll include canary test matrix in the perf plan.

Maya (PM): thanks all. please comment inline on the doc and I'll consolidate. If no major objections, we'll present this at the roadmap sync on Tuesday. :thumbsup:

Chen (Infra): no objections from infra. one ask: include estimated incremental infra $/q for plateau lanes so finance can price.

Sam (Product Ops): +1 to finance ask. also flag legal for KMS controls.

Iris (SRE): will schedule a tabletop evacuation drill after phase 2 prototype.

Maya (PM): I'll send calendar invites after doc update. End of thread.
